evidenceExcerpt: [TRF-016] The ship shall always be loaded down at least to the draught of LIWL amidships when navigating in ice. Any ballast tank, situated above the LIWL and needed to load down the ship to this water line, shall be equipped with devices to prevent the water from freezing. In determining the LIWL, regard shall be paid to the need to ensure a reasonable degree of ice-going capability in ballast. The highest point of the propeller shall be submerged and if possible at a depth of at least h_i below the water surface in all loading conditions. The forward draught shall be at least (2 + 0.00025*Delta)*h_i [m], but need not exceed 4*h_i (2.1), where Delta is the displacement of the ship [t] determined from the waterline on the UIWL (see section 2.1). evidenceExcerpt: [TRF-020] To qualify for ice class IA Super, IA, IB or IC, a ship the keel of which is laid or which is at a similar stage of construction on or after 1 September 2003 shall comply with the following requirements regarding its engine output. The engine output requirement shall be calculated for two draughts by formula 3.1. evidenceExcerpt: [TRF-048] The section modulus of a longitudinal frame shall be calculated using Z = f_4*p*h*l^2/(4*m*sigma_y)*10^6 [cm^3] (4.9). The effective shear area shall be A = sqrt(3)*f_4*f_5*p*h*l/(2*sigma_y)*10^4 [cm^2] (4.10). The bracket shear area shall not be included in the actual frame shear area. Use f_4 = 1 - 0.2*h/s, f_5 = 2.16, p from 4.2.2, h from 4.2.1, s as frame spacing, l as total frame span, m = 13.3 for a continuous beam with brackets unless a smaller factor is required by significantly different boundary conditions, and sigma_y from 4.3.2. | [TRF-053] The section modulus of a stringer situated within the ice belt shall be calculated using Z = f_6*f_7*p*h*l^2/(m*sigma_y)*10^6 [cm^3] (4.11), and the effective shear area shall be A = sqrt(3)*f_6*f_7*f_8*p*h*l/(2*sigma_y)*10^4 [cm^2] (4.12). Use p from 4.2.2, h from 4.2.1, p*h = 0.15 MN/m when the calculated product is less than 0.15 MN/m, l as stringer span, m from 4.4.3, f_6 = 0.9, f_7 = 1.8, f_8 = 1.2, and sigma_y from 4.3.2. | [TRF-054] The section modulus of a stringer situated outside the ice belt but supporting ice-strengthened frames shall be calculated using Z = f_9*f_10*p*h*l^2/(m*sigma_y)*(1 - h_s/l_s)*10^6 [cm^3] (4.13), and the effective shear area shall be A = sqrt(3)*f_9*f_10*f_11*p*h*l/(2*sigma_y)*(1 - h_s/l_s)*10^4 [cm^2] (4.14). Use p from 4.2.2, h from 4.2.1, p*h = 0.15 MN/m when the calculated product is less than 0.15 MN/m, l as stringer span, m from 4.4.3, l_s as the distance to the adjacent ice stringer, h_s as the distance to the ice belt, f_9 = 0.80, f_10 = 1.8, f_11 = 1.2, and sigma_y from 4.3.2.

evidenceExcerpt: [TRF-030] Direct analyses are to be carried out using the load patch defined in section 4.2 (p, h and la). The pressure to be used is 1.8p where p is determined according to 4.2.2. The load patch must be applied at locations where the capacity of the structure under the combined effects of bending and shear is minimised. In particular, the structure must be checked with a load centred at the UIWL, 0.5h0 below the LIWL, and positioned at several vertical locations in between. Several horizontal locations shall also be checked, especially the locations centred at the mid-span or -spacing. Furthermore, if the load length la cannot be determined directly from the arrangement of the structure, several values of la shall be checked using corresponding values for ca. | [TRF-037] The design ice pressure is determined by the formula p = c_d*c_p*c_a*p_0 [MPa] (4.1), where c_d is a factor which takes account of the influence of the size and engine output of the ship. The maximum value is c_d = 1. It is calculated using c_d = (a*k + b)/1000 (4.2).

Note that the main frames below the lower edge of the ice belt must be ice strengthened, see 4.4.1. | [TRF-053] The section modulus of a stringer situated within the ice belt shall be calculated using Z = f_6*f_7*p*h*l^2/(m*sigma_y)*10^6 [cm^3] (4.11), and the effective shear area shall be A = sqrt(3)*f_6*f_7*f_8*p*h*l/(2*sigma_y)*10^4 [cm^2] (4.12). evidenceExcerpt: [TRF-020] To qualify for ice class IA Super, IA, IB or IC, a ship the keel of which is laid or which is at a similar stage of construction on or after 1 September 2003 shall comply with the following requirements regarding its engine output. The engine output requirement shall be calculated for two draughts by formula 3.1. Draughts to be used are the maximum draught amidships referred to as UIWL and the minimum draught amidships referred to as LIWL, as defined in section 2.2. In the calculations, the ship's parameters which depend on the draught must be determined at the appropriate draught, but L and B must be determined only at the UIWL. The engine output shall be no less than the greater of these two outputs. P_min = K_e*(R_CH/1000)^(3/2)/D_p [kW] (3.1), where K_e shall be given a value according to Table 3-1.

evidenceExcerpt: [TRF-016] The ship shall always be loaded down at least to the draught of LIWL amidships when navigating in ice. Any ballast tank, situated above the LIWL and needed to load down the ship to this water line, shall be equipped with devices to prevent the water from freezing. In determining the LIWL, regard shall be paid to the need to ensure a reasonable degree of ice-going capability in ballast. The highest point of the propeller shall be submerged and if possible at a depth of at least h_i below the water surface in all loading conditions. The forward draught shall be at least (2 + 0.00025*Delta)*h_i [m], but need not exceed 4*h_i (2.1), where Delta is the displacement of the ship [t] determined from the waterline on the UIWL (see section 2.1).
